current_answer: As of 12 September 2026 at 12:00 UTC, no broad cross-model core-capability decline is proven. The evidence now includes a quoted GCP Support acknowledgement of a Gemini Deep Research MCP backend failure and a separate repeated Gemini 3.8 Agentic Video tool-processing failure, while Claude Cowork remains the only degraded Claude component in the current status snapshot and Codex telemetry points to higher runtime step frequency and shorter usable allowance windows. These are real changes around specific workflows; they do not establish a broad model-weight decline. Reproduce the exact tool lifecycle, inspect the final served model and artifact, and reconcile allowance before switching or naming capability degradation.

catalogue_card.question: Are popular AI models getting worse right now?
catalogue_card.text: No broad core-capability decline is proven. Google support reportedly traced one Gemini research failure to a backend tool-call regression, while a separate Gemini video path and Codex runtime show real surface and usable-window failures.

summary: A Google AI Developers Forum report says Gemini Deep Research Max and standard preview discover a remote MCP tool but never invoke it; the thread quotes GCP Support attributing the failure to a backend change. Max still writes a report without the private data. This is a serious grounding and product failure, not proof of weaker model weights.

A separate Gemini 3.8 Flash Agentic Video report describes seven of seven full-length files reaching 23 processing calls and 22 results before an internal error, with later attempts returning too-many-tool-calls. It is a repeated tool-loop failure, not a universal 23-call limit or a broad capability test.

Codex runtime telemetry compares five older and five newer high-reasoning Pro sessions: 0.499M to 0.662M tokens per minute, 3.515 to 4.610 steps per minute, and 3.027 to 4.740 observed allowance points per hour. Matched workloads finished about 43% faster, but no answer-quality measure or server ledger is available.

Claude’s current status snapshot lists Cowork on Windows in partial outage while claude.ai, Console, Claude API, and Claude Code are operational. That is a surface-availability finding, not a model-quality score.

Fresh Codex account and Reddit reports describe fast allowance depletion, stuck or slow Astra sessions, and unfinished tasks. They make the usable-window problem worth checking; they do not establish prevalence, server charging, or model decline.

Reader move: record initialize/list/call/result/final events, visible and effective model, surface, route, runtime, effort, context, task outcome, final artifact, retries, tokens, allowance, time, and cost before switching.
uncertainty: The GCP Support acknowledgement is quoted in a community thread with no public fix timeline or incident ID.
The Agentic Video evidence is one report with changed settings, prior longer successes, and no provider response or usage metadata.
Codex telemetry and quota reports are local or self-selected; they lack a server ledger and do not measure answer quality.
Claude status establishes declared component state, not every account experience or model capability.
No public matched longitudinal, cross-provider capability series or first-party audience analytics is available.
